correctness.rationale: The proof derives the triangular difference law from the affine uniform map; direct moment expansion yields three explicit equations. The normalized Gram parameters have exact feasible region 0<p<=1/4 and 0<=q<p, while the normalized moment map has determinant -2952/175. Its exact inverse recovers both side lengths and the unoriented edge angle; affine image gives the stated open-side triangle. The continuum (M2,M4)=(1,2) proves sharpness. The bounded-family Hölder claim follows from the exact inverse and square-root inequality and is sharp near a rectangle. A fresh standalone checker from the packaged path passed 7449 exact arithmetic assertions and an independent 200000-sample numerical comparison; finite testing is corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete sharp moment-space classification of a natural three-parameter convex family under orientation-free sampling. It identifies exactly the finite degree needed to reconstruct all Euclidean moduli, exposes a continuum ambiguity one moment below that threshold, and determines a sharp triangular normalized feasibility region with geometrically meaningful boundary strata. These are motivated finite-statistic inverse-geometric data, not a substitution into a pre-existing finite-inverse theorem. The result is modest in technique but yields a concrete, complete geometric classification useful for checking and inverting population distance statistics.
